To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gut microbiome plays an important role in shaping the brain and its function, and that this is a two-way process, with the brain influencing the gut microbiome.

(i) the gut microbiome plays a critical role in shaping brain development; (ii) changes in the gut microbiome, either directly or via the gut–brain pathway, can induce depressive-like behaviour; (iii) changes in brain function can also alter the gut microbiome; (iv) the gut microbiota can contribute to the pathophysiology of mental illness; and (v) the gut microbiomes of patients with mental illness can be restored by microbiota-targeted therapies.
The gut microbiome plays an essential role in the development of brain circuits and behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the gut microbiome in brain development and mental health.
the role of gut microbiota in shaping the development of the central nervous system, and in the pathophysiology of neuropsychiatric disorders.
how the human gut microbiome can influence neural and cognitive development, and how it can contribute to the pathophysiology and treatment of mental illness.

the gut microbiota is involved in the pathogenesis of mental disorders.
the microbiota is a key component of the brain–gut axis that has a significant influence on brain function and mental health.
